pillars.title: Operational Excellence

criteria.statement: Infrastructure & operations defined as code (no manual console drift).
criteria.notes: 7 chained Terraform modules; secret values set out-of-band, expected not drift.

criteria.statement: CI/CD pipeline exists with automated build/test/deploy stages.
criteria.notes: No CI config anywhere; Phase 4 CI explicitly not implemented.

criteria.statement: Deployments are small, reversible; rollback strategy defined.
criteria.notes: ECR digest pinning enables manual rollback; no written procedure.

criteria.statement: Structured, centralized logging (correlation ids, no secrets in logs).
criteria.notes: Gap: no API Gateway access logs.
Correlation id present; no X-Ray on ingestion Lambdas.

criteria.statement: Actionable alarms tied to SLIs; on-call/notification path defined.
criteria.notes: 5 alarms, alarm_actions defaults to []; gap widened by 2 new alarms.

criteria.statement: Automated tests as a release gate.
criteria.notes: New E2E harness exists; nothing enforces any tier pre-deploy.
Two real incidents recorded only as code comments, not a structured log.
6-widget dashboard, no widget added for new WAF/CloudTrail components.

strengths.text: End-to-end correlation_id threaded through webhook -> SQS -> worker -> runtime.
New 4-phase E2E test ladder specifically targets the managed-infra-IAM failure class that caused two production incidents.
Two live production IAM bugs root-caused, fixed, and documented directly in Terraform comments.
100% infra-as-code across 7 chained Terraform modules.

findings.title: No CI/CD pipeline; fully manual deployment
findings.impact: No automated check would have caught the two live-verified IAM regressions.
findings.recommendation: Add a minimal GitHub Actions pipeline: fmt/validate/pytest on PR, gated plan/apply on merge.

cons: Sequencing 7 chained modules is real work

findings.title: Alarms still have no notification target; gap has widened
findings.impact: 5 alarms including 2 new security ones fire into the void by default.
findings.recommendation: Provision an SNS topic + subscription, default alarm_actions to it.

findings.title: No environment parity
findings.impact: No dev/stage/prod split.
findings.recommendation: Parameterize backend keys; stand up staging.

findings.title: Automated tests not a release gate despite new integration-test capability
findings.impact: The exact managed-infra IAM failure class could still reach production.
findings.recommendation: Wire the unit suite into CI; schedule E2E harness once backend is parameterized.

findings.title: No distributed tracing across Lambda hops
findings.impact: Cross-component analysis depends on grepping correlation_id.
findings.recommendation: Enable X-Ray active tracing on both Lambdas.

findings.title: No API Gateway access logging
findings.impact: Edge-level request logs not captured independently.
findings.recommendation: Add access_log_settings.

findings.title: No post-incident/feedback mechanism
findings.impact: No structured tracking despite 2 real incidents.
findings.recommendation: Start a lightweight incident log.

improvements.text: Create an SNS topic + subscription, wire default alarm_actions (OPS-F2)
Stand up a minimal CI pipeline (OPS-F1, OPS-F4)

pillars.notes: Score moved 57->61: genuine gains from new E2E harness and two documented incident fixes, offset by re-confirmation of CI/alarm gaps (alarm gap widened, not narrowed).

pillars.title: Security

criteria.notes: InvokeRuntimeScoped now a precise 2-ARN list, positive change; remains Partial due to unrelated Bedrock foundation-model wildcard.
AWS-managed keys throughout, incl. new CloudTrail bucket.
No VPC anywhere; PUBLIC network_mode justified.

criteria.statement: No public exposure of data stores.
criteria.notes: Only webhook API public, now double-gated.
CloudTrail+GuardDuty enabled; no notification path; Config/Security Hub absent.

strengths.text: Origin-verify mechanism fully implemented and unit-tested, closing the previously-flagged WAF bypass gap.
InvokeRuntimeScoped IAM fix: precisely-enumerated ARNs, not a reintroduced wildcard.
Genuine account-wide detective baseline: multi-region CloudTrail + GuardDuty.

findings.title: WAF/CloudFront origin-verify closure confirmed; only minimal probing surface remains
findings.impact: No functional bypass; residual exposure limited to cheap 401 rejections against API GW throttle.
findings.recommendation: No further action required at this scale.

findings.title: Detective controls implemented but notification path unwired, Config/Security Hub absent
findings.impact: No alarm/GuardDuty finding routed to a human by default.
findings.recommendation: Create SNS topic, populate alarm_actions; add aws:SourceArn to bucket policy.

pros: Closes gap for all alarms at once

findings.title: No CMK; blocked at account level
findings.impact: AWS-managed keys only.
findings.recommendation: Request narrow kms:CreateKey permissions.

findings.title: Bedrock model-invoke permission scoped wider than models used
findings.impact: Can invoke any foundation model in any region.
findings.recommendation: Scope to specific model ARNs.

findings.title: Unpinned Python dependencies
findings.impact: Builds not reproducible.
findings.recommendation: Pin versions/lockfile.

pillars.notes: Score numerically identical to prior run (81) despite two real improvements, because both land on already-Met criteria rather than the Partial/Missing ones holding the score down. No Critical findings; maturity not capped by this pillar.

pillars.title: Reliability

criteria.statement: No critical single points of failure.

criteria.notes: Only a one-line unqualified DR backlog note.
DynamoDB PITR + state bucket versioning; no restore-test evidence.
Backoff present, no jitter; AgentCore client lacks explicit timeout Config.
DLQ exists but permanent errors swallowed, never reach it (REL-F2).
Rate limiting exists; no circuit breaker.
In-place update, no canary; two prior IAM changes went straight to 100% traffic and broke production.
Unit-mocked only; no infra-level chaos testing -- the exact gap that let both incidents ship undetected.
Single shared worker IAM role/policy; confirmed by the incident halting 100% of async pipeline with zero partial degradation.

strengths.text: Dual-layer idempotency with best-effort release on failure.
AccessDenied-class errors correctly classified as permanent/non-retryable, both live-verified and unit-tested.
DLQ exists, SSE-encrypted, bounded retention.

findings.title: No alarm covers a full silent pipeline stall (the exact failure mode already seen in production)
findings.impact: The confirmed production incident (SQS poller silently failed, zero throughput) would trigger none of the three existing alarms; even a firing alarm has no SNS notification path.
findings.recommendation: Add an alarm on main queue ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage/depth; wire alarm_actions to a real SNS topic.

alternative.summary: Composite alarm (queue non-empty + worker invocations flat) vs. simple queue-age threshold alarm

findings.title: Permanent worker errors dropped without reaching the DLQ or any metric
findings.impact: No ReportBatchItemFailures configured; SQS deletes the whole batch including permanently-failed messages -- zero trace.
findings.recommendation: Enable ReportBatchItemFailures and/or emit an EMF metric for permanent-error counts with its own alarm.

alternative.summary: EMF metric+alarm vs. explicit DLQ send
pros: DLQ send: preserves payload for redrive

findings.title: No blast-radius containment or safe-change mechanism for the shared worker IAM role/deployment
findings.impact: A single IAM role serves 100% of async traffic with no staged rollout; two prior IAM tightenings each independently broke it in production.
findings.recommendation: Add an automated post-apply smoke test invoking the worker Lambda under the real deployed IAM role.

alternative.summary: Lambda alias/CodeDeploy canary vs. scripted post-apply smoke test
pros: Smoke test: cheap, targets exact failure class
cons: Canary: doesn't cover infra-level poller failures, effort L
Smoke test: not wired into CI absent a pipeline

findings.title: Backoff lacks jitter; AgentCore client relies on SDK default timeouts
findings.impact: Concurrent retries can synchronize after a shared throttling event.
findings.recommendation: Add jitter; pass explicit botocore Config timeouts to bedrock-agentcore client.

improvements.text: Add alarm on main SQS queue age/depth, wire alarm_actions to real SNS topic (REL-F1)
Enable ReportBatchItemFailures and/or emit PermanentErrors metric (REL-F2)
Add automated post-apply smoke test for the ingestion module (REL-F3)
Add jitter to retry backoff, explicit timeout Config to AgentCore client (REL-F4)

pillars.notes: One Critical finding (REL-F1) present -- a confirmed production outage of the async pipeline's core throughput, not a hypothetical risk. Maturity capped at 2/5 per the rubric even though the raw weighted score (56) falls in the 3/5 band. REL-08 N/A (no self-managed compute).

pillars.title: Performance Efficiency

criteria.statement: Data store choice fits access patterns.

criteria.notes: CDN caching deliberately disabled for webhook (correct); no DB/LLM prompt cache.
Well tuned incl. new edge-level WAF body-size guard; GitHub client has no connection pooling.
Worker concurrency bounded; local file reads sequential.
Layered bounding incl. new edge-level WAF guards.

strengths.text: Two-tier LLM model selection right-sizes inference cost/latency.
New WAF layer adds genuine edge-level resource-bounding (body-size/rate limit rejected before Lambda invocation).

findings.title: No performance target (SLO) defined for run latency
findings.impact: Latency regressions caught only by manual dashboard inspection.
findings.recommendation: Define SLO, alarm on DurationMs p90.

findings.title: Resource-utilization monitoring omits throttles/concurrency
findings.impact: Saturation invisible except indirectly via queue depth.
findings.recommendation: Add Lambda Throttles/ConcurrentExecutions and DynamoDB throttle metrics.

findings.title: Sequential file reads and Git blob creation
findings.impact: Bounded today, doesn't parallelize as caps grow.
findings.recommendation: Parallelize with bounded thread pool.

findings.title: No HTTP connection pooling for GitHub client
findings.impact: Fresh TCP+TLS handshake per call.
findings.recommendation: Use pooled HTTP client.

findings.title: No LLM prompt caching, no load/benchmark testing
findings.impact: Static prompt resent every run; burst behavior unverified.
findings.recommendation: Enable Bedrock prompt caching; add load test.

pillars.notes: Full re-verification reproduced the same verdict grid as prior run; score independently re-derives to 75. New WAF layer strengthens PERF-12 evidence without changing the verdict.

pillars.title: Cost Optimization

criteria.notes: New WAFv2/CloudFront also pay-per-request with minimal flat fee.
WAFv2 WebACL carries a flat monthly base fee independent of traffic.
New CloudTrail S3/CW retention both bounded.
Extended correctly to new us-east-1 alias provider.
Still absent, slightly more relevant now.
Cheapest CloudFront price class, minimal WAF rule groups.

criteria.statement: Efficient resource use per business value.

strengths.text: End-to-end pay-per-use pricing model for the core pipeline.
New WAF/CloudFront layer kept minimal and cost-conscious.
New CloudTrail/GuardDuty individually toggleable, minimal config, bounded retention.

findings.impact: No proactive alert across a now-larger set of recurring-cost line items.
findings.recommendation: Add aws_budgets_budget and/or Cost Anomaly Detection.

findings.title: No log ingestion sampling control
findings.impact: Negligible at POC volume.
findings.recommendation: Add OTEL sampling if volume grows.

findings.title: No dedicated ephemeral environment lifecycle
findings.impact: Not directly demonstrable.
findings.recommendation: Document teardown approach if a second env is added.

improvements.text: Add aws_budgets_budget scoped to project tag (COST-F1)

pillars.notes: Score moved 82->83 on independent re-check. New WAFv2/CloudFront and CloudTrail/GuardDuty cost surface found well-bounded and justified.

criteria.notes: WAF now filters abusive requests at edge before Lambda.
us-east-1 for WAFv2 is a hard AWS constraint, not discretionary.

Add storage-class transition to CloudTrail bucket (SUS-F2)

criteria.notes: Locking still Missing across all 6 S3 backends.

pillars.title: Decoupling

criteria.notes: New origin-verify handshake is additive, not a violation.
Shared table (DEC-F3) plus implicit SQS-poller coupling (DEC-F1).
Terraform chain requires strict apply order, fails safe.

strengths.text: SQS main+DLQ decouples webhook ingress from worker processing.
New origin-verify secret is clean single-source-of-truth injection.

findings.impact: A prior least-privilege tightening silently broke the pipeline via this invisible dependency.
findings.recommendation: Document the managed-poller IAM dependency explicitly; add regression protection.

findings.title: No alarm on main-queue backlog/age
findings.impact: None of the three existing alarms would catch this failure signature.
findings.recommendation: Add alarm on ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage.

findings.title: Shared DynamoDB table with no documented key-schema contract
findings.impact: Two components read/write one table with only informal key-naming separation.
findings.recommendation: Document the contract or split into two tables.

findings.title: No explicit contract versioning on the async payload
findings.impact: A breaking rename could fail silently.
findings.recommendation: Add schema_version field.

findings.title: ORIGIN_VERIFY_SECRET fails open when unset
findings.impact: Deliberate for local/test use; not exploitable today.
findings.recommendation: Add Terraform precondition against empty secret.

improvements.text: Add alarm on main SQS queue age (DEC-F2)

pillars.notes: No Critical/High findings. The SQS-poller IAM bug primarily affects DEC-04 (hidden coupling via managed infrastructure), not DEC-06 (no synchronous cascade occurred).
